title: Taking relief for an embedded ball
question: If your ball is embedded in the ground after landing in the fairway, what are you allowed to do according to the rules?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies, even though it is embedded.
Pick it up, clean it, and drop it within one club-length of its original spot, not nearer the hole, with no penalty.
Take a two-stroke penalty and drop it anywhere on the green.
Replace it exactly where it is embedded, without cleaning it.

explanation: If your ball is embedded in the fairway, you may lift, clean, and drop it within one club-length no nearer the hole without penalty.
imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer prepares to drop his golf ball near the spot where it was embedded in the fairway.
imageAlt: Boy golfer ready to drop his ball next to where it was embedded on the fairway.

imageVerification.repairPrompt: Ensure the golfer is clearly left-handed by using the left hand (from the viewer's perspective, right side of image) to drop the ball if not already unambiguous.
